A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inverse Attention research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations across five MPE games, population-scale and attention-prediction analyses, and a five-participant human study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds larger-population, partial-observation and gradient-field ablation experiments in Appendices A.6–A.8.

M1.justification: The core architecture and three-phase training procedure remain. Appendix A.7 adds a limited inference adaptation: applying inverse attention only to observable agents. Appendix A.8 introduces a raw-position ablation without replacing the main model.

E1.justification: Appendix A.7 extends evaluation from fully observable environments to restricted-visibility scenarios across all five games. This substantially broadens input-environment coverage; the underlying games and human-study population remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparators remain. The new 10-10 scalability comparison includes IPPO, MAA2C and ToM2C*, absent from v1's population-scale tables. Table 13 also introduces Inverse-Att-Vanilla as a direct ablated comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments extend Grassland to ten sheep and ten wolves, test visibility radii of 1.5, 1.0 and 0.5, and replace gradient fields with relative positions for Inverse-Att-Vanilla while retaining gradient-field inputs for baselines. These substantially expand tested conditions and controls; existing training budgets, splits and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.7–A.8 add restricted-visibility robustness tests and a gradient-field removal ablation, addressing sensing limitations and representation contributions. Appendix A.6 extends the existing scalability analysis to twenty agents. Earlier attention-prediction, multiple-Inverse-Att and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The three-seed statement and all existing mean-and-uncertainty entries remain unchanged. Newly added studies report point estimates without uncertainty estimates in Tables 10–13, introducing less complete uncertainty reporting; this does not establish any change in run counts.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–6 and Figure 4 are unchanged. Tables 10–12 add substantial results for larger populations, restricted visibility and raw-position inputs. For example, Table 10 reports Inverse-Att rewards of -52.34 and 132.39 for Grassland sheep and wolves. Table 13 combines new ablation scores with retained full-model scores, rather than showing a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (6) changes an explicitly named L2 loss into unspecified norm bars around a comma-separated target/prediction pair. The unchanged surrounding explanation does not resolve whether this is faulty notation or an intended mathematical change. Other formal definitions and derivations remain, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: inferring other agents' attention, using it to adjust actions, and improving adaptation to unfamiliar agents and humans. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes partial-observation adaptability to attention's handling of variable inputs and emphasizes gradient fields' contribution. However, the claim of consistently best partial-observation performance overstates Table 11: at radius 1, Grassland sheep score -20.41 for Inverse-Att versus -2.26 for Self-Att. Existing same-agent-type and variable-population limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the code-availability sentence and repository link from v1's abstract without providing a replacement. Existing hyperparameters, data splits, synthetic-data generation and minimum hardware requirements remain. Appendix A.8 additionally specifies which agents receive raw positions versus gradient-field inputs.

R1.justification: v2 removes Cheng et al. (2023) and Tang et al. (2022), replacing the latter's introductory citation with the already cited Tang et al. (2020). The main Theory-of-Mind and ad-hoc teaming positioning remains. Song's changed year and publication information refer to the same work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained with copyediting. v2 pluralizes the title, enumerates baselines, makes limitations a subsection, moves references after the appendix, and removes Broad Impact and Acknowledgement sections. Existing human-study and resource appendices are retained and renumbered. Equations (5)–(7) introduce literal 'dots' typesetting errors.

P2.justification: Tables 10–12 add substantial new result displays, including a three-block visibility comparison; Table 13 juxtaposes ablation and retained full-model scores. The conference layout enlarges Figure 2, relocates tables and reformats Table 6's header. Existing figure content is largely retained. Table 11 incorrectly repeats the Grassland 10-10 caption despite displaying visibility experiments.

improvement.justification: The gradient-field ablation makes component contributions more assessable, while visibility and twenty-agent tests add useful applicability evidence absent from v1. These benefits are limited by missing uncertainty in the new results, the contradicted blanket claim accompanying Table 11, less clear loss notation, and removal of the code link. The original empirical results and central claims remain unchanged.
